question: Can an additional identity observation detect a wrong mapping after conditional model confidence has crossed 95%?
outcome: 48 new systems yield 576 conditions and 4,032 audit records. Under 70% administrative change, a two-identity audit chosen by the frozen posterior rejects all 60 wrong proposals; a random two-identity audit rejects 56. Correct proposals all pass. A conservative random rule has an exact conditional probability bound of at most 5% for accepting a wrong map, with one wrong acceptance in 288 administrative proposals. All 12 independent review checks pass.
challenge: Model confidence can stop on a wrong map, while verification cost and selection affect detection. A rejection leaves the mapping unresolved. The first verifier contained an unnecessarily complex code-availability expression and a redundant assertion.
remedy: Frozen proposals were checked against separately acquired identities; exact uniform-subset probabilities were enumerated. System-level paired summaries retain all size conditions. The original review was preserved and a simpler verifier replayed the same checks and results.
retry_when: Specify measurement errors, sequential proposal correction or multiple generative models in a fresh protocol; acquire an archaeological observation with an independently justified identity likelihood.
